comment: Package kit hints for Remote access (docs/package-testing.md «Module kit file»). No demo data: the seed makes a folder, two computers, a gateway, an application, a shared credential and one journal entry through the module's own API. Every address is 127.0.0.1 on ports 9–12 (nothing listens there; a computer's address + port is unique): guacd is not configured (guacdHost empty), so the session the seed starts is written to the journal and answered GUACD_OFF without any connection, then ended — no real host, guacd or VNC agent is contacted. The links are the WebSocket tunnels the package attaches to the HTTP server (ctx.onHttpServer), probed at the HTTP level with a forged token only. `enhances: directory` (AD import) has no API link to probe.

apiParams.id: SELECT id FROM remote_hosts ORDER BY id LIMIT 1

links.name: guacd tunnel answers its upgrades (forged token → 401)
links.oldCoreWhy: Built-in Remote of v1.20.0 attaches both ws servers with { server, path }; the Portal VNC one answers 400 to every upgrade not on its path, so the guacd tunnel never gets its upgrades there (fixed in the package: upgrade.js routes one listener). The old core is only checked for an answer below 500.

links.name: Portal VNC tunnel answers its upgrades (101, closed on the forged token)

openToUsersWhy.sessions: the person's own sessions and the ones on their own computer (transparency: everyone sees who connected to them)

plainUserWhy: The plain user (no remote.* right) opening /app/remote directly sees the module's own «no access» state: its bootstrap GET /api/app/remote answers 403 and the page handles it (the launcher does not list the module for them). The kit lists that API 403 as a warning.
